audit_question: Audit the provided deck set: ShadowPriest, CtAPaladin, PirateRogue, BigShaman, Discolock, TreantDruid, ImbueMage, MechPala, Kingslayer, Boarlock, PirateDH, and CuteWarrior. Verify which decks are representative matrix controls, which remain source-informed, and whether CuteWarrior should stay supplemental to avoid widening the matrix too early.

primary_sources.evidence: Defines the representative 11-deck HSConfig proof set and marks fixture_stage per deck.
States the matrix is the representative 11-deck proof set, requires closing Kingslayer and Boarlock before widening, and says CuteWarrior is supplemental.
Lists CuteWarrior with proof_role supplemental_command_acceptance, matrix_policy not_representative_until_kingslayer_boarlock_closure_review, and operator_action keep_supplemental.
Locks total_decks=11, core_source_backed_fixture_count=9, source_informed_valid_fixture_count=2, and the normal next action to close existing source-informed rows before adding more decks.
Locks the representative matrix at 11 rows, requires one Kingslayer row, one Boarlock row, and zero CuteWarrior rows.
Confirms CuteWarrior is not a representative matrix row and must remain supplemental.
Uses CuteWarrior at runtime_prepare stage as a blocked supplemental example instead of a representative fixture.
Passed with 16 tests on 2026-07-08, confirming the matrix counts, source-informed blockers, and promotion policy used in this audit.

confirmed_facts: The representative HSConfig matrix currently contains 11 decks, not 12.

Nine provided decks are representative matrix controls with fixture_stage core_source_backed_fixture: ShadowPriest, CtAPaladin, PirateRogue, BigShaman, Discolock, TreantDruid, ImbueMage, MechPala, and PirateDH.
Two provided decks remain representative but source-informed rather than strong controls: Kingslayer and Boarlock.
Kingslayer remains source_informed_valid_fixture with first_strongness_gap needs_mulligan_claim_for_quick_pick and closure priority 2.

Boarlock remains source_informed_valid_fixture with first_strongness_gap needs_mulligan_claim_for_fracking, multiple blocking reasons, and an explicit stop condition exact_boarlock_fracking_mulligan_source_unavailable.
CuteWarrior is not part of the representative matrix and is intentionally tracked in supplemental-proof-decks.json as supplemental_command_acceptance.
Operator policy explicitly says not to add a new representative deck when an existing row already covers the same source-depth or runtime-surface family.
Operator policy explicitly says to close or review the current Kingslayer and Boarlock source-informed rows before widening the matrix.
The provided deck set therefore splits into three groups: nine representative matrix controls, two representative source-informed rows, and one supplemental non-matrix deck.
strengths: The current matrix is lean and explicitly bounded at 11 representative decks.
Each representative deck has a documented fixture stage and strongness visibility status.
The matrix already covers broad mechanic families without promoting CuteWarrior prematurely.
Kingslayer and Boarlock remain visible as honest source-informed controls instead of being misreported as source-backed strong.
Supplemental policy cleanly separates narrow command-acceptance proof decks from representative coverage decisions.
gaps_or_risks: Kingslayer is still blocked on exact Quick Pick mulligan evidence, so it cannot yet be treated as a strong representative control.
Boarlock is still blocked on exact Fracking mulligan evidence plus runtime-surface and coverage gaps, so it remains a durable source-informed control rather than a closed strong row.
Promoting CuteWarrior into the representative matrix now would widen the matrix without resolving the two known source-informed gaps, which would dilute the current closure discipline.
The matrix purpose is lean pre-game CustomConfig coverage, so it still has documented limits around reactive control, discover chains, and some exact combo cases depending on the deck.

representative_source_informed_rows.first_missing_chain: DEEP_014 Quick Pick needs mulligan claim

supplemental_only.reason: It proves narrow command or syntax behavior without changing the representative matrix count and should not become a twelfth representative row before Kingslayer and Boarlock closure or explicit review.

deck_set_implications.overall_conclusion: The provided deck set is already the intended current audit set: nine strong representative controls, two honest source-informed representative rows, and CuteWarrior as supplemental support. Keeping CuteWarrior supplemental preserves the lean matrix and keeps attention on closing the existing source-informed truth gaps first.

recommendation: Keep the representative matrix unchanged. Treat ShadowPriest, CtAPaladin, PirateRogue, BigShaman, Discolock, TreantDruid, ImbueMage, MechPala, and PirateDH as the current representative matrix controls; keep Kingslayer and Boarlock as the only source-informed representative rows; and keep CuteWarrior supplemental until Kingslayer and Boarlock are either closed to source-backed strong or explicitly reviewed as durable long-term source-informed controls.
